title: Rebound-Attack Security with Multiple Inbound Stages
summary: Strong partial-round differential bounds would leave few characteristic-satisfying pairs, but proving security against rebound attacks with multiple inbound stages remains open.

formal_statement.body: For rebound attacks on a permutation, determine whether differential-characteristic bounds over a smaller portion of the permutation can yield a provable security argument when the attack uses multiple inbound stages. Although a sufficiently strong bound over a fraction of the rounds would imply that only a small number of pairs satisfy a differential characteristic, it remains unresolved whether interactions among multiple inbound stages invalidate this pair-scarcity reasoning. The required result is a rigorous proof of security against rebound attacks that accounts for these multiple inbound stages and their effect on the differential-characteristic bounds.

scope.domain: Differential cryptanalysis of rebound attacks on permutations using partial-round differential-characteristic bounds.
parameters: Partial permutation portion: the fraction of rounds over which differential-characteristic bounds are considered
Multiple inbound stages: the attack components whose interactions may affect pair-scarcity reasoning
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish a rigorous security proof against rebound attacks that accounts for multiple inbound-stage interactions and their effect on differential-characteristic bounds.

citations.label: Bounds in Shallows and in Miseries

progress.summary: The source notes that sufficiently strong bounds on a fraction of the rounds would imply that few pairs satisfy a characteristic, but identifies multiple inbound stages as a possible failure point. It explicitly leaves a provable security argument against rebound attacks open.
